quiz.q: What does a foreign key guarantee?
options: The value points at a row that really exists in another table
quiz.explain: REFERENCES makes Postgres refuse values that don't exist in the other table.

quiz.q: How do you model books ↔ tags (many-to-many)?
options: A tags text column in books
A third table holding (book_id, tag_id) pairs
A foreign key from tags to books
quiz.explain: A join table like book_tags stores one row per pairing.

options: Postgres picks the id and you can't override it by accident
quiz.explain: Postgres numbers rows itself; inserting your own id is refused unless you say OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE.

quiz.q: Deleting an author who still has books fails because…
options: The foreign key's default rule refuses to leave books pointing at nothing
quiz.explain: By default a foreign key blocks deleting a row that others still reference.

flashcards.back: Put a foreign key column on the 'many' side (books.author_id → authors.id).
JOIN keeps only matches; LEFT JOIN keeps every left row, with NULLs where nothing matches.
